title: It feels right.
paragraphs:
It feels right.
It must be right.
That’s the lie.

“Follow your heart,” they said.
But Jeremiah 17:9 cuts through the noise like a blade:
“The heart is deceitful above all things and desperately sick—who can understand it?”

Not weak.
Not confused.
Deceitful.

We don’t like that verse.
Because it confronts the one thing we trust the most—ourselves.

Your heart can feel love… and lead you into lust.
It can crave freedom… and drag you into bondage.
It can whisper “this will make you happy”… while quietly destroying your soul.
And here’s the tension:

Your feelings are real.
But they are not reliable.
But here’s what we miss…

God never told you to follow your heart.
He told you to guard it.

Proverbs 4:23:
“Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.”

Guard it—from lies.
From unchecked desires.
From voices that sound like truth but aren’t.

Because if your heart is the compass…
and it’s broken…
you won’t end up where you think.
And that’s where grace walks in.

God doesn’t leave you trapped in a deceitful heart.
He offers you a new one.

Ezekiel 36:26:
“I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you.”

Not repaired.
Replaced.

Through Jesus Christ—His death, His resurrection—your old, wandering heart can be made new.
Not driven by impulse, but led by truth.
Not enslaved to desire, but anchored in Him.
So no—don’t follow your heart.

Lead it.
Submit it.
Surrender it to Christ.

Because the safest place your heart can be…
is not in your feelings—
but in His hands.
From deception to redemption—because Jesus rewrites everything.
